correctness.rationale: For every existing real Hadamard H of order n>=2 with exactly one flipped sign, normalizing the row/column defect gives a two-mode matrix and an (n-2)-dimensional singular-value block. A trace/nuclear norm weighted polar witness yields the sharp lower bound and a positive Gram factor X with constant diagonal and B^T X^{-1}B=X gives the global complex Schur multiplier upper bound gamma_n=((n-2)sqrt(n)+2(n-1)sqrt(n+2))/(3n-2). The n=2 special case is a rank-one sign matrix multiplier of norm 1. Independent Sylvester 4,8,16 calculations verified the positive Gram certificate and upper/lower equality at machine precision; they do not prove the unbounded n claim.

value.rationale: A single-sign error is the most natural robustness test of sharp Schur norms for Hadamard matrices. The exact all-existing-order deficit, independent of equivalence class and defect location, quantifies a nontrivial stability phenomenon, improving beyond an isolated order-four calculation. The explicit global factorization and orthogonal lower witness are useful for operator-theoretic Schur norms.
